 Oral Judgment

1. The present appeal is filed by the original claimant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 28/09/2012 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.),
Kachchh at Bhuj in MACP No.373 of 1999.

sentences.text: That on 12/01/1999, when the applicant was going on his moped bearing registration no.GJ-12-A-3968 from Anjar to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2852/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined

Gandhidham, opponent no.1 came from opposite direction with ST Bus bearing registration no.GJ-18-V-982 of opponent no.2 driving the bus in rash and negligent manner and thereby went on wrong side of the road and dashed with the moped of the applicant and caused accident in which the applicant sustained serious injuries over various parts of his body.
Therefore, he filed claim petition under the provisions of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act against the opponents seeking compensation of Rs.3,50,000/-.

3. Vide the aforesaid impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the present appellant-original claimant under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the present appellant-original claimant is entitled to an amount of 85,200/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the same, present appeal has been filed by the appellant- original claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. This Court vide order dated 26/09/2013, noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellant- original claimant and the grounds raised in the present appeal, has admitted the appeal.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation to the claimant and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true perspective.

It is also submitted NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2852/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined that the Tribunal has not properly assessed the income of the injured claimant and has overlooked the settled principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in relation to the assessment of conventional heads such as medical expenses, pain, shock and suffering, proper diet, attendant charges, transportation etc.
The learned counsel has urged that the compensation awarded is not just, fair, and reasonable, and is liable to be enhanced in accordance with the settled legal principles.

5.1. Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant has assailed the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and submitted that the amount awarded under various conventional heads are also on the lower side.
Learned advocate has invited the attention of the Court to the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal on the aforesaid issue.

He has submitted that looking to the injury sustained by the claimant as well as the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157,
future prospects of income is required to be taken into consideration.

sentences.text: 6. Learned advocate for respondent no.2-Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation has submitted that the claimant has not produced iota of evidence to prove his income.

She has further submitted that whenever there is no any income proof produce by the claimant, the court must consider the rate of minimum wages and the tribunal has therefore, considered income of the claimant appropriately.

She has further submitted when income of the claimant is not proved, the claimant is not entitled for future loss of income and submitted that tribunal has awarded just, proper and reasonable amount of compensation and the same is not required to be interfered by this Court in this appeal and lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal.

7. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass and perused the material documents available on record and the impugned judgment and award, more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while considering the issue of quantum of compensation.
8.

As regards the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellant on the assessment of the income of the injured claimant is concerned, the Tribunal has considered Rs.2,000/- as just income considering the nature of work the claimant was doing at the time of accident and age of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2852/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined claimant.
9.

As regards the future prospects, considering age of the claimant and injury sustained by him, 25%
future prospects is required to be considered.
Accordingly, considering as the same, monthly income of the claimant would come to Rs.2,500/- (Rs.2,000/- x 25%).
Thereafter, considering functional disability of 20%, loss of monthly income would come to Rs.500/-.
As rightly recorded by the Tribunal, the claimant was aged 45 years at the time of accident and hence, multiplier of 14 is appropriate.

Lastly, the amount to be awarded under other conventional heads is also required to be reconsidered as the claimant suffered the injuries which caused permanent disability to some extent to the claimant and thereby he suffered pain accordingly and some amount under the head of amenities of life is also required to be considered.

10. Therefore, original claimant-appellant herein is entitled to enhanced amount as computed hereunder:
